memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land. When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of that area, saw her, he took her and raped her. His heart was drawn to Dinah daughter of Jacob; he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her. And Shechem said to his father Hamor, 'Get me this girl as my wife.'" - Gen 34:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This chapter opens with a terrible wrong. Dinah goes out to visit the local women, and Shechem, a powerful man, seizes her and violates her. The Bible states it plainly and does not soften it: this was an assault, a grievous evil done to an innocent young woman.

We must be clear about something the world often gets wrong: this was in no way Dinah's fault. She was the victim of another person's sin. The Scripture places the blame squarely where it belongs — on Shechem, who abused his power to harm her.

Notice, too, how the passage exposes a counterfeit "love." After the assault, we read that Shechem's heart was "drawn" to Dinah, that he "loved" her and wanted to marry her. But love does not seize and violate; love honours, protects, and never takes by force. Whatever Shechem felt, it began with a crime against her, and no later feeling could undo that wrong.

If you carry wounds from such a violation, hear this gently: what happened to you was not your fault, and God is not indifferent to it. He is close to the brokenhearted (Ps 34:18), and He is a God of justice who sees every wrong. This is a painful topic, and God's heart burns against the abuse of the vulnerable. He does not overlook it, and in His time He will set all things right.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I understand that the victim of abuse is never to blame?
2. How does it comfort me that God sees and cares about every injustice?
3. Where do I need to entrust a deep wound to the God who is near?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are close to the brokenhearted and just toward the oppressed. Comfort all who have been wounded by evil, and assure them it was not their fault. We trust You to bring justice in Your time. Amen.
